# TTU System and Fermi America Announce the World’s Largest Advanced Energy and Intelligence  Campus

![Fermi America - Campus Rendering](https://www.texastech.edu/images/fermi-2.jpg)

_Rendering courtesy of Fermi America_

June 26, 2025 \| Contact: [Kristina Butler](mailto:kristina.w.butler@ttu.edu)

The Texas Tech University System (TTU System) announced a collaboration with leading
energy and technology company [Fermi America](https://fermiamerica.com/) on Wednesday (June 25) to create one of the most significant power campuses in the
U.S. and the largest advanced energy, private grid and intelligence development in
the world.

Located on approximately 5,800 acres in the Texas Panhandle, an area with a long history
of energy production and a solid foundation of natural resources, the Advanced Energy
and Intelligence Campus will support the growing demands of artificial intelligence
(AI), data innovation and sustainable energy.

The site will include 18 million square feet of data centers and generate up to 11
gigawatts of IT capacity from natural gas, solar, wind and clean nuclear energy, providing
a comprehensive solution to the demands of AI innovation.

![Rendering courtesy of Fermi America](https://www.texastech.edu/images/fermi-4.jpg)_Rendering courtesy of Fermi America_

Texas Tech University (TTU) and the TTU System have been dedicated to serving the
Panhandle and the West Texas region for 75 years. Through this collaboration, the
TTU System and Fermi America will continue to uphold and expand on that unique responsibility.

“The Texas Tech University System is proud to partner with Fermi America on this historic
endeavor,” said Chancellor Tedd L. Mitchell, M.D. “Texas is the energy capital of
the world, and this campus will not only be the largest energy and data complex of
its kind, but also a testament to the unshakable spirit of our system, the Texas Panhandle
and this great state.”

Through this ambitious project, Fermi America, co-founded by former U.S. Energy Secretary
and Texas Governor Rick Perry, will provide critical infrastructure energy solutions
through cutting-edge technology and proven world-class multidisciplinary leadership,
positioning the U.S. as a global leader in the energy-intensive AI race.

“The Chinese are building 22 nuclear reactors today,” said Perry. “We’re behind, and
it’s all hands on deck. President Trump’s first executive order spoke to the energy
issue and how we must continue to make America energy dominant. No one does energy
better than Texas, and Fermi America and the Texas Tech University System are answering
the call.”

In addition to the energy and technology components, the project will also advance
the mission of the TTU System by providing academic and research opportunities for
faculty and students, including internships, employment and workforce training and
placement programs that will benefit all five TTU System institutions. The plan also
includes the construction of an academic and research facility featuring office, classroom
and conference spaces.

![Rendering courtesy of Fermi America](https://www.texastech.edu/images/fermi-3.jpg)_Rendering courtesy of Fermi America_

Fermi America is committed to furthering the development of the TTU System by supporting
an excellence fund to enhance strategic priorities, promote academic excellence, advance
research and ensure student success.

“This collaboration will not only position Texas Tech to address the evolving demands
of the energy and technology sectors but will also create meaningful educational opportunities
for our students and research possibilities across many disciplines for our faculty,”
said TTU President Lawrence Schovanec.

**About Fermi America**

[Fermi America](https://fermiamerica.com/) is a leading energy development company that powers the future of artificial intelligence.
Co-founded by former U.S. Energy Secretary Rick Perry, Fermi America combines cutting-edge
technology with a deep bench of proven world-class multi-disciplinary leaders to create
the world's largest, next-gen HyperGrid™ a first-of-its-kind behind-the-meter campus that will combine the largest nuclear
power complex in America, the nation’s biggest combined-cycle natural gas project,
utility grid power, solar power, and battery energy storage to deliver hyperscaler
data capacity, providing critical infrastructure energy solutions that will power
the future of artificial intelligence (AI).

**About the Texas Tech University System**

Established in 1996, the Texas Tech University System is one of the top public university
systems in the nation, consisting of five universities – [Texas Tech University](https://www.ttu.edu/), [Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center](https://www.ttuhsc.edu/), [Angelo State University](https://www.angelo.edu/), [Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center El Paso](https://ttuhscep.edu/) and [Midwestern State University](https://msutexas.edu/).

Headquartered in Lubbock, Texas, the TTU System is a more than $3 billion enterprise
focused on advancing higher education, health care, research and outreach with approximately
21,000 employees and 64,000 students, more than 400,000 alums, a statewide economic
impact of $19.2 billion and an endowment valued at $3 billion. In its short history,
the TTU System has grown tremendously and is nationally acclaimed, operating at [21 academic locations](https://www.texastech.edu/campuses.php) in 17 cities (15 in Texas, 2 international).

In addition, the TTU System is one of only nine in the nation to offer programs for
undergraduate, medical, law, nursing, pharmacy, dental and veterinary education, among
other academic areas.
